task.description:
BACKEND-DEV already wrote real tests (test-ddl-validate: 20 unit tests; test-integration-mig04-mig05: 9 tests; test-integration-mig06: 6 tests). Write tests/specs/DDL-01.md, tests/specs/MIG-04.md, tests/specs/MIG-05.md, tests/specs/MIG-06.md per test_developer_guide.md format, tracing every AC (read full bodies from docs/requirements.yaml) to specific existing test cases. Pay special attention to MIG-05 AC5 -- CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR already accepted that this AC is satisfied by process/tooling discipline, NOT runtime code, so there should be NO test claiming to cover AC5 with an assertion (that would be testing something that does not exist) -- instead document in the spec why AC5 has no test (mirroring how MIG-02 AC5 was handled as a structural/non-testable note in batch 0). Close any genuine coverage gap you find for AC1-4 of MIG-05 or any AC of DDL-01/MIG-04/MIG-06 by adding a test.

REWORK 1 (routed by ORCH after TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR Step 3b FAIL):
- [BLOCKER] tests/integration/migration_resume_test.zig::TC-MIG-04-03 ("resume's tenant snapshot query plan uses platform_migrations_resume_idx") fails deterministically -- zig build test-integration-mig04-mig05 is genuinely 8/9, not the claimed 9/9. The test runs EXPLAIN against a migration_id with ZERO fixture rows seeded before the EXPLAIN, so Postgres's planner correctly picks a sequential scan over an empty/near-empty table instead of the partial index -- the index itself (migrations/1144_platform_migrations_control_table.sql:38) is correct and exists; this is purely a test-fixture defect. Fix: seed enough matching (status IN ('pending','failed')) fixture rows for this test's own migration_id BEFORE running EXPLAIN, so the planner has a genuine reason to prefer the index scan. Re-verify zig build test-integration-mig04-mig05 is a real, reproducible 9/9 (run it twice) before reporting PASS.
acceptance_criteria: tests/specs/DDL-01.md, MIG-04.md, MIG-05.md, MIG-06.md exist and trace every AC to a specific test case or a documented non-testable/out-of-scope note
MIG-05 AC5 explicitly documented as non-runtime-testable (accepted design decision), not silently ignored
Any genuine coverage gap closed with a new test case
No error.SkipZigTest on any MUST-requirement test
